title: Correct churchite-(Y) irradiation table references
body:
Independent review confirmed a minor source-locator error in `data/records/churchite-y.yaml` at SHA256 `5d4560f2f71d0e79f280c99919c9aa07c62fbca47f723611b8becbb9090e5cc5`.

Both the `xenon_irradiation_amorphization` mechanism description and its first evidence explanation cite **Table 3** for Y-churchite critical amorphization fluence. In the complete original Rafiuddin et al.2026 article, DOI[10.1021/acs.inorgchem.6c01299](https://doi.org/10.1021/acs.inorgchem.6c01299), Table3 contains rhabdophane curve-fit parameters. **Table4**, *Fc and Tc of Hydrous and Anhydrous Rare-Earth Phosphates*, contains the YPO4·2H2O row with3.1×10^13ions/cm² and0.03dpa. Original Figure13 bottom row independently agrees with those values.

The numerical result, synthetic dihydrate identity, model-versus-measurement distinction and abiotic scope are supported; this is not a change to the scientific conclusion.

Preserved native observation: `20261015T023705Z-churchite-y-round86-table-locator-initial`, finding `F1`, stable key `churchite-y-round86-irradiation-table-locator`. Original JATS SHA256 `16e50844f4ca5f42ebaeefa83e2b4a50892a61ae38636ed28c44e8ecf6e9a1a1` and original full HTML are bound there; no failed main-PDF route is treated as evidence.

Acceptance:

- Correct both irradiation references to Table4; preserve unrelated Table2 synthesis references and source values.
- Correct any dossier locator repeating this error, retaining exact before/after provenance.
- Append canonical EDIT and inline history; preserve CREATE and initial native observation.
- Pass affected validation and save an independent successor explicitly resolving this exact F1/key/previous occurrence against final owner bytes.

Exact frozen dossier occurrences are also confirmed: Markdown line23 and JSON ['claims', 1, 'locators', 3]. Companion /private/tmp/cmm-round86-churchite-independent/20261015T023840Z-dossier-locator-occurrence.json binds their original hashes; preserve those originals and append a correction dossier pair.

title: Clarify phosphorus accounting and endpoint inconsistencies in the municipal-sludge study
body:
Pradhan et al. (2021), *Phosphorus Recovery from Sewage Sludge Using Acidithiobacilli*, DOI [10.3390/ijerph18137135](https://doi.org/10.3390/ijerph18137135), provides complete primary evidence for culture-associated acidification and a filtered-liquid phosphorus endpoint. Its quantitative attribution remains unresolved.

The inspected official 13-page PDF (SHA256 `814f0989066848ac230444a798bf5180cf3788a950e449228013e9e84a7e2a11`) identifies phosphate, iron and trace-element additions in the growth-medium recipes (§2.4), repeated sludge replacement (§2.6), and source-reported phosphorus inventories/solubilization percentages (§3.3, Table 5 and Figure 2). An explicit nutrient-input subtraction and closed replacement/sampling balance were not found. Some Table 6 elemental percentages exceed 100%, and some Figure 1 final-pH traces do not match Table 5.

Follow-up work:

- Locate original raw assay/blank data, a correction or an author-supplied clarification through legitimate public routes; do not infer missing controls or silently repair printed values.
- Resolve medium-derived phosphorus and trace metals versus sludge-derived material, actual liquid/sludge replacement and sampling volumes, and percentage denominators.
- Reconcile Figure 1 endpoint labels with Table 5 and verify whether the reported 92% phosphorus endpoint is reproducible from source measurements.
- Preserve indigenous growth in uninoculated-medium controls, the 63-day sequential design and the distinction between filtered soluble P and isolated product recovery.

Acceptance requires a cited original clarification or reproducible source calculation with all necessary inputs. Until then, retain the qualified observation and uncertainty in the record. This is a source-evidence follow-up, not a claim that the current scoped record is defective. Hidden/ignored-inclusive exact DOI/title/author searches of records, research, reviews, histories and the initial all-state issue inventory found no duplicate issue in the inspected bounds.

title: Acquire complete heterogenite bioleaching originals before adding microbial claims
body:
The new heterogenite owner accepts explicitly abiotic ALTA2023 mixed-ore leaching. It does not yet accept the microbial pyrite-assisted route described in:

- Zeka, Lambert, Frenay, Gaydardzhiev and Ndala (2015), *Possibilities for Co(III) dissolution from an oxidized ore through simultaneous bioleaching of pyrite*, Minerals Engineering75:54–62, DOI[10.1016/j.mineng.2014.12.023](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.mineng.2014.12.023).
- Related2016 IMPC contribution, *The role of bacteria and the addition of pyrite during leaching of Co(III) from heterogenite*, [official ORBi record](https://orbi.uliege.be/handle/2268/202467). Its experimental overlap with the2015 paper is unresolved.

On2026-10-15 the [official2015 repository record](https://orbi.uliege.be/handle/2268/176113) was accessible, but its advertised `1-s2.0-S0892687514004300-main.pdf` bitstream redirected to a request-copy HTML form. The2016 `impcPaper466.pdf` did likewise. Both non-PDF responses and exact hashes/times are preserved under `/private/tmp/cmm-round86-sulfides-research`; no request or author contact was sent. Abstracts/metadata are insufficient to verify phase characterization, inoculum/strain, reagent doses, controls, replication, full analytical methods or denominator.

Acceptance:

1. Obtain complete legitimate main originals and any relevant supplements, recording actual file types, routes, dates and hashes. A request-copy form or indexing snippet is not the original.
2. Inspect all claim-bearing figures/tables, mineral/ore characterization and controls. Preserve mixed-feed scope, unassigned polytype where relevant, cobalt valence evidence, ferric/ferrous/pyrite changes and any abiotic comparator limits.
3. Verify organism/strain or community resolution from actual methods; do not assign causal roles from taxonomy alone.
4. Resolve2015/2016 experimental lineage and retain source contradictions. Distinguish elemental mobilization from isolated-product recovery and laboratory outcomes from deployment.
5. Add only supported claims through a history-bearing owner EDIT and independent native review; otherwise retain an explicit source deferral.

Round86 all-state issue search found no existing heterogenite/Zeka DOI issue. Existing#238 concerns different antimony originals and#248 rambergite; neither is resolved by this work. The paired round86 heterogenite source dossier contains exact acquisition and deduplication evidence.

title: Resolve zinc-silicate phase and composition evidence gaps
body:
The round86 willemite and hemimorphite owners preserve narrower supported claims. This follow-up should remain open until original evidence resolves the following limits; it is not a claim that either source is generally unavailable.

1. **Hemimorphite-like microbial precursor:** Medas et al. 2018, DOI10.2138/am-2018-6128, original p719 identifies deposit AM-18-56128 through the official May2018 MSA contents page. The complete nine-page original is inspected (SHA256 `32071969c68b1925ab922fc7517f55e8bc611cb46d637b31b44685576fc99df7`), but the supplement was not acquired through the bounded routes recorded in the dossier. Obtain that legitimate deposit, inspect S1–S3/TableS1, and determine whether the diffraction, fitting and chemistry justify anything stronger than the present low-order hemimorphite-like precursor context. Obtain the complete separate Medas2017 aging paper (DOI10.1016/j.oregeorev.2017.07.015) before adopting its conversion or solubility measurements. Do not promote field association to controlled microbial necessity.
2. **Synthetic willemite composition:** Xu et al. 2022, DOI10.3390/met12122031, §2.1/Table1/Figure1 describes a pure synthetic willemite feed but reports Zn48.7–49.5wt% and SiO234.8–36.5wt%, unlike ideal Zn2SiO4 (approximately58.7wt%Zn/27.0wt%SiO2). Complete20-page original SHA256 `61515b8beb61fee33715541ef127460deb959a9981d1bf89710f250577d1aa4a`. Resolve the analytical basis or original assay/diffraction data before accepting purity, phase-specific conversion or a closed mass balance. The presently reported79.78% remains aqueousZn relative to assayed feedZn, not a recovered mineral/metal yield.

Acceptance: retain legitimate source URL and actual raw byte hashes, independently inspect the missing or corrected original data, document experimental lineage, and amend records only where new evidence supports a change. Save canonical EDIT history and a linked independent review for any scientific revision. Preserve the present qualifiers if the gap remains unresolved. No author contact is authorized by this research draft.

Handoff: `research/sources/round86-zinc-minerals/20261015T023418Z-source-investigation.{json,md}`. The all-state issue inventory was searched for these exact DOIs/deposit and candidate names within the recorded bounds; parent should perform final live issue deduplication before posting.
